headline: Google commits ≥€13bn to Finland AI infra with Fortum nuclear PPA; raids hit Berlin SPD Spitzenkandidat Krach; Tailwind joins Shopify.

stories.title: Google: ≥€13bn Finland AI infra + Fortum nuclear life-extension PPA

facts.text: Google (9 Sep): plans to invest at least €13bn in Finnish digital infrastructure over 2027–2028 — sites in Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos, Vaala — calling it its largest single Europe investment.
22-year Fortum PPA supports Loviisa nuclear life-extension beyond 2030 (~10% of Finland’s electricity; ~580 plant jobs). MoU also covers new flexibility / potential new Loviisa reactors.
Extra clean power: onshore wind PPAs (Valorem, Suomen Hyötytuuli) bringing Google-supported new-to-grid wind to 629 MW; 94 MW battery near Kajaani targeted late 2027.
Construction-phase estimate: ~€3.6bn average annual GDP contribution and >37,000 nationwide jobs (incl. ~16,000 construction); once operational ~7,000 jobs. €31m community fund over four years.
Package framed as Google’s largest single Europe investment; includes clean-energy PPAs and community funds alongside the data-centre build-out.

stories.whyItMatters: Nordic AI/data-centre race meets grid politics — Google is buying long nuclear visibility, not just land and fiber.

stories.title: Raids hit Berlin SPD Spitzenkandidat Steffen Krach

facts.text: ZDFheute / StA Hannover (Wed ~18:14): prosecutors confirm searches at three sites in Hannover and Berlin tied to Bestechlichkeit suspicions against SPD Spitzenkandidat Steffen Krach.

Reporting links the case to the former Krankenhaus Lehrte / Regionsklinikum Hannover rebuild; Krach pushed the shift as Regionspräsident and chaired the clinic supervisory board until his Berlin candidacy.
Tagesspiegel: Schöneberg flat + SPD Landesgeschäftsstelle (Wedding) searched; Region Hannover confirms Hannover office rooms. Krach is on leave from the Regionspräsident role.
Krach calls the claims haltlos “Unterstellungen,” says he has nothing to hide and will cooperate (RBB / SPD Berlin statement). Unschuldsvermutung applies; AGH vote is 20 Sep.

stories.whyItMatters: Less than two weeks before Berlin’s Abgeordnetenhaus election — a direct hit on the SPD’s top candidate while polls already have the party in single digits.

stories.title: Tailwind Labs is joining Shopify

facts.text: Adam Wathan (9 Sep): Tailwind Labs is joining Shopify so the framework has a “stable long-term home” — CSS still MIT-licensed; team keeps leading the OSS projects.
Claimed install volume: >110M downloads/week; named users include ChatGPT, X, Cloudflare, Reddit, and Shopify itself.
Commercial shift: existing Tailwind Plus / ui.sh customers keep access; new signups close so the team can focus on Tailwind inside Shopify (storefronts, admin, Shop app, agentic commerce).
HN spike: ~525 points / ~203 comments by evening window.

stories.whyItMatters: One of the default CSS stacks just got absorbed by a commerce giant — maintenance path is clearer; independent Tailwind-as-business is over.

stories.title: US escalates Canada fight to product import bans

facts.text: tagesschau (Wed AM): Trump decrees ban Canadian dairy, alcohol (beer/whiskey/wine), and motorcycles/mopeds from entering the US from 29 Sep — official says single-digit billions in trade value.
From 15 Sep: +50% tariffs on more Canadian goods (mattresses, motorboats, golf carts). Federal procurement told to drop Canadian firms (hits IT / office suppliers).
Context: overnight Canadian counter-tariffs (up to 50%) on US steel/alum, appliances, ag equipment, pulp/paper, electronics — Canada cites ~$27.6bn of US goods. Prior US Aug tariffs covered ~$20bn.
Trade talks had already collapsed; LeBlanc says Ottawa will talk if the US engages in good faith and respects Canadian sovereignty.

stories.whyItMatters: Beyond tariff tit-for-tat — outright bans plus a procurement freeze harden a North American trade break ahead of US midterms.

stories.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday: 974 CVEs, two exploited Windows zero-days

facts.text: Rapid7 (8 Sep Patch Tuesday): Microsoft publishes 974 own-product CVEs (723 Windows) — most CVEs Microsoft has ever shipped in a single day; +25 non-Microsoft CVEs → 999 on the table.
Exploited in the wild: CVE-2026-85880 (Windows ALPC EoP → SYSTEM via buffer overflow / OOB write) and CVE-2026-81963 (Windows Update Stack EoP via improper link resolution).
ALPC patch note: Server 2025 / Win11 reportedly not listed for CVE-2026-85880 — Rapid7 reads that as possible Rust memory-safety payoff on newer kernels.
Separate from this afternoon’s Android Sep bulletin (remote priv-esc without taps) — Windows shops still need the Update Stack + ALPC fixes.

stories.whyItMatters: Volume Patch Tuesdays are the new normal; two already-exploited EoPs mean prioritize before the next ransomware chain.
